channel.title: POLITICO Pulse
channel.description: Delivered daily by 10 a.m., Pulse examines the latest news in health care politics and policy, with special editions from the 2026 Milken Institute Future of Health Summit, Nov. 10–13.

item.title: Hospitals and Dems rally to reverse Medicaid cuts
item.description: With Democrats set to control Congress in January, hospitals hope lawmakers could be persuaded to undo some of the Medicaid cuts that Republicans passed last year.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Can Stephen Miller save MAHA?
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Healthy Again movement has been in dire need of a win after an especially embarrassing midterm season in which MAHA voters failed to be the electoral force Republicans hoped for. Now, they think they’ve found their victory.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Dem health care priorities take shape
item.description: Congress is back in session this week, and Democrats have begun laying the groundwork for the health-related policies they plan to pursue when they have control of both chambers next year.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: A defining moment for RFK Jr.
item.description: This week, a U.N. body is set to consider whether the U.S. can still say it eliminated measles. For vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the decision could define his legacy as health secretary.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper

item.title: A Kennedy critic atop oversight panel?
item.description: Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee and a fierce critic of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., is angling to lead the committee come January.
